Modified assessment incorporating literature: The statement is modestly hawkish. The FOMC raised the target range to 4.50–4.75% and signals “ongoing increases,” consistent with rules-based guidance like the Taylor rule and with determinacy results from estimated policy rules (e.g., Lubik and Schorfheide 2004) that call for a more-than-one-for-one response to above-target inflation. The emphasis on achieving a “sufficiently restrictive” stance and continued balance-sheet runoff aligns with credibility-focused frameworks (Goodfriend 1991, 1993) and with evidence that Fed actions affect term premia and the yield-curve slope (Cochrane; Piazzesi). The explicit attention to policy lags and data dependence tempers the hawkishness at the margin. The historical precedent of the Volcker disinflation underscores the Committee’s reaffirmed commitment to restoring inflation to 2%. Net tone: slightly more hawkish than neutral, though less hawkish than earlier in the cycle due to acknowledgment that “inflation has eased somewhat.”
